    I also found and fixed a real cleanup miss: the remote branch docs-1528-skill-codex-m1 had survived my earlier teardown. I confirmed its tree was byte-identical to the
    squash-merge before deleting it, and fast-forwarded local main from ed53a30e to 2625da53. No m1 branch or worktree remains in either repo.

    The thing you need to know: the v1 reap took the P4 evidence

    You ruled the no-liveness reap deliberate and I accepted that — the v1 verb dies in the same release, so a live v1 team's state is dead weight. That reasoning covers
    coordination state. It does not cover the work products, and those are gone.

    ~/.adaai/state/flock/fl-20261004-3oe8/ went from 148 entries to 7. What survives is only cursors/architect.json, events.jsonl, lock.watcher, watcher-state.json and watcher.log.
    Deleted with no copy anywhere on the machine:

    - All five P4 records — p4-run-results.md, p4-run2/3/final-results.md, p4-1531-acceptance-record.md
    - All six P4 run databases (p4-run1-v1.db … p4-run4-2fb0ead1.db)
    - Every review and PR-body file the team produced, plus bodies/ — the full text of every message this team exchanged

    I searched ~/.adaai and ~/Dev for all of it. Nothing. These were never committed and never posted to GitHub, so the P4 acceptance evidence for #1531 is unrecoverable from this
    machine. The GitHub side is intact — #1568 and #2476 findings live in their PRs, the T9a and lead-notify histories are in #1571 and #1573 — but the measurement record itself is
    what is lost.

    I did not reconstruct the P4 record from memory. A record I cannot source is worse than a missing one, and inventing one to fill a gap is exactly the failure mode this whole
    epic is built to prevent. I also did not re-create files in the old v1 path, since that root is now reaped on every update and anything placed there is lost the same way.

    Reported as done on ref 1575 with the flag in the body; the architect was woken (seq 74). I've asked for a ruling: accept the loss and say so in the epic close, or authorise a
    re-measurement against v2. The second is new work, so I'm not starting it unasked. Standing by.
